title: Wesley So tops Jerusalem Masters, bags P6.4 million
summary: Cavite-born Wesley So captures his fourth chess title this year, saying he plays best when 'ultra relaxed'

blocks.text: NEXT MOVE. Wesley So in action at the 2026 Jerusalem Masters.
Cavite-born Wesley So captures his fourth chess title this year, saying he plays best when 'ultra relaxed'

MANILA, Philippines – Filipino-American Super Grandmaster Wesley So notched pulsating back-to-back wins to claim the Jerusalem Masters 2026 title and $101,000 (P6.4 million) late Thursday, November 26, at the Museum of Tolerance in Israel’s capital.

Striking in his last listed major tournament for the year, the Bacoor, Cavite-born So bested Russian Alexey Sarana in the deciding Armageddon for a 3-2 victory in the final of the 12-man all-GM tournament.
They wound up tied after two rapid games and two blitz tiebreakers.
In the semifinal, the 33-year-old So tamed fellow Team USA member Hans Moke Niemann, also via Armageddon when he secured a draw with black.
So clinched his fourth crown this year, including his fourth United States championship, the GCT (Grand Chess Tour) Sinquefield Cup, and the American Cup.
“I’m very happy, no more pressure,” said So in the post-game interview. So disclosed in the semifinals that he plays best when “ultra relaxed” and free from result pressure.

After the round-robin qualifying stage, So was tied with Sarana at 7.0 points, trailing defending champion Arjun Erigaisi, with 9.0 points, and Niemann, with 8.0 points. Russian top seed Ian Nepomniachtchi tallied 6.5 points and missed the knockout semifinals.
It was a remarkable recovery for So, who finished 13th out of 24 participants in last week’s Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest, Hungary.
If any consolation, So fared better than perennial world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen, who landed 17th.
Following his Jerusalem triumph, So gained 10 points and climbed to ninth in the FIDE Live Rapid rating. So is ranked sixth in classical play. – Rappler.com
